header.userPrompt:
Fix GitHub issue #5542: remove the `phase` attribute from the OpenTelemetry `http.server.request.duration` histogram, so that it is recorded exactly once per request, as the OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions require (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/http/http-metrics/#metric-httpserverrequestduration).

## Problem

Both OpenTelemetry metrics modules record the `http.server.request.duration` histogram twice per endpoint-handled request: once in `onResponseHeaders` with attribute `phase=headers`, and once in `onResponseBody` with `phase=body`. `phase` is not part of the semantic conventions, `count` of the histogram is ~2x the number of requests, and cardinality doubles. It is not exactly 2x: `onException` records once with no phase attribute, `onInterceptorResponse` records once with `phase=body`, so filtering on `phase=body` on the user side drops exception observations.

Affected files:
- metrics/otel4s-metrics/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/otel4s/Otel4sMetrics.scala (`requestDuration`, `responseAttrs`)
- metrics/opentelemetry-metrics/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/metrics/opentelemetry/OpenTelemetryMetrics.scala (`requestDuration`, `asOpenTelemetryAttributes` for responses)

The label originates from the Prometheus metrics (2022), where it must stay: Prometheus, Datadog and ZIO metrics use tapir-specific metric names and are NOT in scope. Do not touch them.

## Required changes

1. In `requestDuration` of both modules: remove the `onResponseHeaders` callback. Record the histogram once, on `onResponseBody`, plus the existing `onException` and `onInterceptorResponse` paths. Never add a `phase` attribute.
2. Remove the now-constant `phase: Option[String]` parameter from `Otel4sMetrics.responseAttrs` (package-private, used by the test) and from the response overload of `OpenTelemetryMetrics.asOpenTelemetryAttributes` (private).
3. `MetricLabelsTyped.forResponsePhase` / `ResponsePhaseLabel` in server/core must stay (other backends use it). Add a short note to its doc comment that the OpenTelemetry modules (`OpenTelemetryMetrics`, `Otel4sMetrics`) ignore it.
4. Update the doc comments on `OpenTelemetryMetrics.default` (two overloads) that currently describe the `phase` attribute; remove those sentences.
5. Tests:
   - `metrics/otel4s-metrics/src/test/.../Otel4sMetricsTest.scala`: `requestDurationExpectation` success branch expects `pointCount(2)` with `phase=headers` / `phase=body` points; change to a single point without a phase attribute. Remove the `phaseAttribute` helper. Adapt the `responseAttrs` call sites to the new signature.
   - `metrics/opentelemetry-metrics/src/test/.../OpenTelemetryMetricsTest.scala`: asserts `AttributeKey.stringKey("phase")` at ~lines 167 and 291; update so the duration histogram has one point per request, no phase key.
   - Add or adjust a test in each module that verifies the duration histogram's `count` equals the number of successful requests (this is the user-visible bug).
6. Docs: doc/server/observability.md — the OpenTelemetry and otel4s sections do not mention phase; verify and leave as is. Do not create a migration doc.
7. PR description must state this is a breaking change for anyone querying the OpenTelemetry duration histogram by `phase`, and reference `Fixes #5542`. Keep the PR description short and in simple language.

## Constraints

- Comments: only add what is not obvious from the code, keep them minimal.
- Compile and run tests for the Scala 2.13 and Scala 3 variants of the two modules: `sbt "opentelemetryMetrics/test" "opentelemetryMetrics3/test" "otel4sMetrics/test" "otel4sMetrics3/test"` (sbt-projectmatrix ids; `opentelemetryMetrics` also has a 2.12 variant, `opentelemetryMetrics2_12`, which must compile too).
- Do not add Claude as a co-author on commits.
